title: Synthetic load harness for profile regression and origination trace
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Build an automated synthetic load harness and trace origination metadata for verified performance profiles. The harness will replay representative request mixes (latency-sensitive vs throughput-heavy) across model variants and collect deterministic fingerprints: p50/p90/p99 latency, throughput curves at load points, and normalized cost-per-token. Origination traces will capture the model binary, quantization, hardware SKU, kernel set, and profile commit hash to enable reproducible regression investigation.
background: We have frequent small perf regressions surfaced by ops and customers after model updates or runtime kernel tweaks. Current verification relies on ad-hoc runners and manual traces, which makes triage slow and pin/rollback decisions risky. Existing profile artifacts lack an easy way to reproduce the exact environment that produced them.
proposed_solution: 1) Implement a configurable harness that can run synthetic traffic according to scenarios (short-chat, long-context generation, embedding bursts) and produce a structured CSV/annotated log of metrics. 2) Integrate an origination tracer that attaches: model version, profile git SHA, runtime kernel fingerprint, hardware SKU, quantization parameters, sequence-length distribution sample, and cost model version. 3) Publish harness outputs as part of the perf profile release artifact and surface a 'replay' button in the Console to reproduce historical profiles in a staging queue.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): design harness scenarios and implement basic runners for text-generation and embeddings with offline logging. Phase 2 (2 weeks): add the origination tracer, standardize artifact schema, and wire artifact publishing into the profile publish pipeline. Phase 3 (2 weeks): Console integration with a replay job UI and internal alerting for profile regressions. Start with internal models and a single GPU SKU, then expand.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run three canonical scenarios and emit stable p50/p90/p99 and throughput vs load curves
Origination tracer fields are recorded for every run and included in profile artifact metadata
Published profile artifact stored in canonical registry with replayable manifest and link to run logs
Console shows a replay control that queues a staging job with the exact origin fingerprint
At least one historical regression reproduced using the harness and traced to a kernel selection change
